chapter: Savoy days, the Concord and business
title: The Savoy: Goodman-Webb battle and the swinging floor
summary: He describes the crowded block and the floor bouncing at the Goodman-Webb battle.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: And, I wanted to ask you to sort of give us a general impression. You have hinted a few times about the kind of an environment that you found at the Savoy in terms of the battles of the bands and all of that going on, and, if you could sort of paint a picture for us of what that whole era was like in terms of the various bands. Not only the ones that we mentioned, but even Benny Goodman's band came up from time to time, I understand, you know, to join in back and forth.
And, of course, your band and Chick Webb's Band.
I remember the time that Chick Webb and Benny Goodman, they was at that time — is that it? [Second tape records]
Yeah. That's it. Yeah. Excuse me, Erskine. You were talking about the environment and the band battles and things at the Savoy.

Yes. They used to have one of those nights. Well, I remember one night when Benny Goodman and Chick Webb had a battle of music, they called it. You couldn't get nowhere on that block. And now to show you how crowded it was, I'm working there and I couldn't even get in to hear them. I couldn't get through that front door. That was a beautiful, that was a beautiful scene. You'd get up there and the people were always packed up there in front of the bandstand. And the Savoy Ballroom had a floor what you'd call a swinging floor. And then the people, if people get in the groove, and the band would get in the groove, people would be going up and down. You could see that whole floor, crowd of people going up and down. That was a beautiful scene. And then, they also had something like taxi dances through those years too. Well, on nights like that, there wasn't no room for them. You know?
